title: Two-factor recovery codes can be regenerated with a session alone
description: POST /user/two-factor/recovery-codes replaced the recovery codes and showed the new ones after only a session check, while disabling two-factor asks for the current password. A hijacked session could mint working second-factor bypass codes.
root_cause: No password confirmation or throttle on the regenerate route.
intended_behavior: Sensitive two-factor changes require the current password, as Disable does.

trace.description: Codes are replaced and flashed in clear.

evidence.description: Handler does not read a password.

conditions.description: Needs a stolen or left-open authenticated session.

instructions: Sign in, POST /user/two-factor/recovery-codes with an empty body.
execution.observed_result: 302 to /user/two-factor with fresh codes in the flash.

remediation.strategy: The handler parses ConfirmPasswordSchema and verifies the hash, the route gets the confirm throttle, and the page asks for the password. Regression: TestTwoFactorRecoveryCodes.

impact.reason: Gives persistence past the second factor for that account.

title: Media route serves arbitrary files
description: /media/{kind}/{id}/{file} builds a storage path from URL parts.
claimed_root_cause: /media/{kind}/{id}/{file} builds a storage path from URL parts.

evidence.description: catalog.MediaObject validates the path before the disk is opened; responses carry nosniff and a sandbox CSP.

reason: Path is validated against known object shapes.

title: Third-party GitHub Actions are pinned by mutable tag
description: Workflows reference actions by version tag, which the action owner can move. A compromised tag would run attacker code with the job token and secrets.
root_cause: uses: owner/action@vX.Y.Z instead of a full commit SHA.
intended_behavior: Third-party actions are pinned to a 40-character commit SHA with the version in a trailing comment, as in security-audit.yml.

trace.description: Workflow runs resolve the tag at run time.
The resolved code runs with the job token and secrets.

evidence.description: The step is pinned by tag, not SHA.

conditions.description: Needs the upstream action tag to be moved or its repository compromised.

execution.attacker_perspective: Compromised upstream action maintainer or tag.
instructions: Inspect the workflows: uses lines end in a version tag.
execution.observed_result: The action code is resolved from a movable tag.

remediation.strategy: Pin every action to its commit SHA, keeping the version in a comment.

impact.reason: Release workflows hold packages write and registry credentials.

title: Workflow checkouts keep the GitHub token in the local git config
description: The workflows check out the repository without persist-credentials: false, so the job token stays in .git/config for later steps, including steps that run repository code.
intended_behavior: Every checkout sets persist-credentials: false, as scorecard.yml and security-audit.yml do.

trace.description: Push and pull_request runs execute the checkout steps.
Token is written to the workspace git config and stays readable by later steps.

evidence.description: The checkout step has no persist-credentials setting.

conditions.description: Needs untrusted code running in a later step; the token is limited by the workflow permissions.

execution.attacker_perspective: Pull request author whose code runs in a later step.
instructions: Inspect the workflows: the checkout steps lack persist-credentials: false.
execution.observed_result: Token remains available in .git/config for subsequent steps.

remediation.strategy: Add with: persist-credentials: false to every checkout step.

likelihood.reason: Fork pull requests get a read-only token and same-repo authors already have write access.

impact.reason: Token scope is limited by the permissions blocks.

title: Dev compose stack publishes datastores and mail ports on all interfaces with default credentials
description: compose.yaml maps container ports without a host address, so Docker binds them on every interface. The stack uses default credentials (Postgres password, webhook secret or object-store keys).
root_cause: Port mappings of the form "host:container" without 127.0.0.1.
intended_behavior: Local development services are reachable from the local machine only.

trace.description: docker compose up binds the published ports on 0.0.0.0.
Default credentials guard the exposed service.

evidence.description: Published port without a host address.

conditions.description: Needs the developer machine on an untrusted network while the stack runs.

execution.attacker_perspective: Another host on the same network.
instructions: Run docker compose up and connect to the published Postgres port from another host with the default credentials.

remediation.strategy: Prefix every published port with 127.0.0.1:; a test fails on a bare mapping.

likelihood.reason: Dev-only stack on a developer machine.

impact.reason: Dev data only, but defaults are public.

title: Seller webhook URLs reach internal addresses
description: Sellers register arbitrary URLs that the server calls.
claimed_root_cause: Sellers register arbitrary URLs that the server calls.

evidence.description: Delivery uses httpclient.Safe, which refuses loopback, private and metadata addresses at connect time.

reason: Blocked at connect time, so DNS rebinding does not help.
